# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Under the AI Act as originally enacted, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (medium confidence). However, the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, postponed this application date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, related deadline for Annex I product-embedded high-risk systems has also shifted, though sources disagree on whether the new date is 2 August 2027 or 2 August 2028.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As originally enacted in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026 (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf). A separate source describes a 36-month timeline (around August 2027) rather than 24 months, creating some inconsistency in characterizations of the original schedule (medium confidence) [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Deadline
The AI Omnibus amended the AI Act's timeline, entering into force on 27 July 2026, and moved the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Digital Strategy — AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). A consolidated version of Article 113 confirms that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems), except Article 6(5), shall apply from this date (medium confidence) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113).

Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 on the Commission's proposal to adjust the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, with application tied to confirmation that necessary standards and conformity tools are available (medium confidence) [Council of the EU press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). One official source states the Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement followed on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Digital Strategy — AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). A lower-confidence source identifies the implementing instrument as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (low confidence) [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

### Related Transitional Provisions
Under amended Article 111(2), the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before Chapter III's application date only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward; providers/deployers of systems used by public authorities must still take necessary preparatory steps (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk — Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111).

### Annex I Product-Embedded Systems
Under the amended timeline, obligations for AI systems classified as high-risk because they are embedded in regulated products under Annex I will apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy — AI Omnibus](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). One source instead states this transition extends only to 2 August 2027 (low confidence) [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act).

### Pre-Omnibus Commentary
Commentary published before the Omnibus entered into force (around April 2026) described 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III obligations, reflecting the pre-amendment law (low confidence) [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- Several sources still cite 2 August 2026 as binding, reflecting outdated pre-Omnibus law, while the majority of authoritative sources confirm the extension to 2 December 2027 [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation).
- Sources disagree on the Annex I product-embedded deadline: 2 August 2027 versus 2 August 2028 [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (flagged as low confidence).
- The claimed sequence of Omnibus "adoption" (19 November 2025) preceding "political agreement" (7 May 2026) is internally inconsistent and unclear (flagged as low/medium confidence) [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) vs. [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules).
- The identification of "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" as the amending instrument is low confidence and unverified against primary legal sources [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether further delays beyond 2 December 2027 are possible if harmonised standards remain unready.
- Whether 2 December 2027 applies uniformly across all Annex III-related duties (e.g., registration, post-market monitoring) or only to core Chapter III obligations.
- Clarification needed on terminology inconsistencies between "entry into force" and "application date" across secondary sources.
- Confirmation of the correct Annex I product-embedded deadline (2027 vs. 2028).

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Under the AI Act as originally enacted, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (medium confidence). However, the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, postponed this application date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, related deadline for Annex I product-embedded high-risk systems has also shifted, though sources disagree on whether the new date is 2 August 2027 or 2 August 2028.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As originally enacted in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026 (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf). A separate source describes a 36-month timeline (around August 2027) rather than 24 months, creating some inconsistency in characterizations of the original schedule (medium confidence) [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Deadline
The AI Omnibus amended the AI Act's timeline, entering into force on 27 July 2026, and moved the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Digital Strategy — AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). A consolidated version of Article 113 confirms that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems), except Article 6(5), shall apply from this date (medium confidence) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113).

Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 on the Commission's proposal to adjust the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, with application tied to confirmation that necessary standards and conformity tools are available (medium confidence) [Council of the EU press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). One official source states the Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement followed on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Digital Strategy — AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). A lower-confidence source identifies the implementing instrument as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (low confidence) [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

### Related Transitional Provisions
Under amended Article 111(2), the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before Chapter III's application date only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward; providers/deployers of systems used by public authorities must still take necessary preparatory steps (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk — Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111).

### Annex I Product-Embedded Systems
Under the amended timeline, obligations for AI systems classified as high-risk because they are embedded in regulated products under Annex I will apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy — AI Omnibus](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). One source instead states this transition extends only to 2 August 2027 (low confidence) [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act).

### Pre-Omnibus Commentary
Commentary published before the Omnibus entered into force (around April 2026) described 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III obligations, reflecting the pre-amendment law (low confidence) [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- Several sources still cite 2 August 2026 as binding, reflecting outdated pre-Omnibus law, while the majority of authoritative sources confirm the extension to 2 December 2027 [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation).
- Sources disagree on the Annex I product-embedded deadline: 2 August 2027 versus 2 August 2028 [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (flagged as low confidence).
- The claimed sequence of Omnibus "adoption" (19 November 2025) preceding "political agreement" (7 May 2026) is internally inconsistent and unclear (flagged as low/medium confidence) [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) vs. [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules).
- The identification of "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" as the amending instrument is low confidence and unverified against primary legal sources [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether further delays beyond 2 December 2027 are possible if harmonised standards remain unready.
- Whether 2 December 2027 applies uniformly across all Annex III-related duties (e.g., registration, post-market monitoring) or only to core Chapter III obligations.
- Clarification needed on terminology inconsistencies between "entry into force" and "application date" across secondary sources.
- Confirmation of the correct Annex I product-embedded deadline (2027 vs. 2028).
